transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate your time. Um... well, I hope I'm not overreacting by coming in, but... I guess what finally scared me into actually making this appointment is... well, it's a little hard to admit, and I really don't want you to get the wrong idea, but I've been having some unsettling thoughts. 

Just sort of... thinking things like, if I didn't wake up tomorrow, maybe that would just be easier. I absolutely do not want to hurt myself, I promise you that, I really don't! It's just... having those thoughts kind of startled me, and I didn't want to ignore them. Am I making sense? I just wanted to make sure I was doing the right thing by getting it checked out, if that's alright.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you normally like doing?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I really don't want you to think I've just given up or anything, because I am still trying to keep busy. I still set out my paints, or I'll think about going to my pottery class... but, um... it's just that lately, when I actually sit down to do it, I just sort of stare at the materials. I just don't seem to feel any of the spark I used to feel. 

I feel a little guilty even admitting that out loud, because I know I should be enjoying it, and I really am trying to push through. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Have you been feeling like you’re a failure or that you’ve let people down, or maybe been blaming yourself for things more than usual?

Oh, um... well, I really try to stay positive, and I know everyone makes mistakes, but... I guess I have been a little hard on myself lately. I hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent, because I really do care about my job at the store and I always try my best. 

But I'll catch myself just... replaying these tiny little mistakes in my head. Like, if a display sign I set up is just a little crooked, or if one of the new trainees looks even slightly confused when I'm explaining something, I just... I start telling myself that I'm a completely useless supervisor. Which I know is probably silly, because I've been doing this a long time and my managers usually say I do good work! It's just... I've been feeling so guilty over the absolute smallest things right now, like I'm letting everyone down. 

Is it normal to get that hung up on stuff like that? I really hope I'm not just overthinking it all and wasting your time.
Have you noticed feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

Well, um... I guess I have been feeling a bit down. I really try to start my day with a smile, especially since I need to set a good example for the team at the store, but... it's been a little tough lately. 

Most mornings, I just... I wake up with this heavy, sort of gray feeling. It's almost like all the color has just drained out of everything before I even get dressed for work. I usually try to just put on a brave face and push through it, because I don't want to bring anyone else down with me. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a downer or anything. I really do try to stay cheerful for the customers. Does that make sense? I'm sorry if I'm not explaining it very well.
Have you noticed that you’re feeling more tired or that you’ve been lacking energy lately, even when you haven’t done anything physically or mentally exhausting?

Well, um... I really don't want to sound lazy, because I've always prided myself on being a hard worker, you know? I try to keep moving and stay productive... but, yes, I suppose I have been feeling pretty worn out lately. 

I hope you don't think I'm just making excuses, but even when I get a full night's rest, I just... I wake up feeling so drained. It's like the simplest things take everything out of me. Just doing my normal routine, like unlocking the doors to open the store, or answering a couple of questions from the staff... or even just carrying my groceries inside when I get home. It just feels so exhausting right now. 

I really am trying to push through it and keep up with everything, though. I hope that's the right answer... does it make sense to feel that tired from such little things?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like eating much less or much more than usual?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I really try to make sure I eat my regular meals, you know, to keep my strength up for the store. I haven't really noticed my clothes fitting any differently or anything like that. 

I mean, maybe sometimes I don't have a huge appetite when I first wake up with that... that heavy feeling I mentioned, but I always make sure to force down at least some toast or oatmeal so I'm not running on empty. I hope that's okay? I really do try to take good care of myself so I can keep doing my job properly and not worry anyone. 

Is it... is it a good sign that my eating has stayed pretty normal? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed that you’ve been moving more slowly than usual, or maybe fidgeting or restless without meaning to?

Well, um... I try really hard to always look professional and composed, especially in front of my team at the store. But... I guess if I'm being completely honest, there have been some things. I feel a little silly admitting this, because I know I should be setting a better example, but... some days I do catch myself just pacing around my living room at home. And I've been picking at my cuticles a bit, which I know is a terrible habit. I'm really trying to stop doing that, I promise. 

And then... other days, it's almost the exact opposite. Like, even just walking from the break room back out to the sales floor feels... I don't know, strangely slow. Like I'm walking through water or something. I always try to pick up the pace and smile if a customer is looking, though, so I don't think it's affecting my work too much. 

Is that... is that the sort of thing you're asking about? I hope I'm explaining it right, and I'm sorry if it sounds like I'm a bit all over the place.
Have you found that you’re not interested in absolutely anything, or that you’re not able to enjoy even the things you used to really like?

Well, um... I really try to keep my hobbies up, because I know how important it is to have a good work-life balance, right? I don't want to just be all about the store. So I still set out my paints on the weekends, or I'll think about going down to my pottery class... 

But, I don't know, it's a little embarrassing to admit... lately, when I actually sit down with the paints or get to the class, I just sort of... stare at the materials. It's like that spark I used to feel is just... missing right now. I still go through the motions, though! I really do try to stay engaged and not just sit around. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound ungrateful for the free time I have. I'm sure it's just a phase and I'll get my enthusiasm back soon. Does that... does that answer your question okay?
Have you found that you’re not interested in absolutely anything, or that you’re not able to enjoy even the things you used to really like?

Oh, um... I think that's sort of what I was just trying to explain about my artwork. I'm so sorry, did I not make sense before? Let me try to be a little clearer! 

Like I was saying, I really do still make the effort to set out my paints, or I'll get myself all the way down to the studio for my pottery class. I know I should be having fun doing those things. But... yes, when I actually get there, I just kind of end up staring at the clay or the canvas. That spark I used to get from being creative, it's just completely gone right now. 

I really am trying my best to push through it, though, and not just give up. Is that... does that give you a better idea of what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, um... I really don't want to sound like a complainer, because I know everyone goes through rough patches, right? But... I guess this low, flat sort of feeling... it's been hanging around for about six months now. 

I've really been trying to push past it, I promise. But it's been long enough that my usual routines, like the art classes I mentioned, or even my morning walks... they just stopped feeling restorative. I keep doing them because I know I should, but... yeah, it's been about half a year. 

I'm so sorry if that seems like a long time to let something go before getting help. I really thought I could just work through it on my own. Is... is six months a normal amount of time for this sort of thing?
Have you ever felt this way before, like this low or down for a long period of time, or is this the first time you’ve experienced something like this?

Well, um... I really hope I'm remembering this right, because I want to give you the most accurate answer. But, gosh, looking back... I don't think I've ever felt quite like this before. 

I mean, of course I've had days where I felt a little blue or stressed from work—retail can be pretty demanding, especially around the holidays, you know? But I always bounced right back. This... this heavy feeling that just won't lift, where even my paints don't cheer me up... I really think this is the first time it's stuck around like this. 

I'm sorry, I hope that's helpful. Does that make sense, that it would just sort of show up now for the first time?

Have you ever had a period of time where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or extremely confident, even if others around you seemed concerned about your behavior or thought you were acting out of character?

Oh, um... well... I really don't want you to think I'm a difficult person to work with, because I usually pride myself on being a very cooperative supervisor. But... I guess, right before this whole slump hit, there was a little stretch where I was feeling... oh, I don't know, maybe a bit *too* sure of myself? 

I had all this drive for the store, but looking back, I wasn't being very pleasant. I'm a little embarrassed to admit this, but I would actually snap at people over just tiny little comments. Like, my district manager was just asking a standard question about some of the visual layouts I had set up, and I just completely bit her head off over it. 

Which is so unprofessional of me, I promise! I'm normally very good at taking feedback and being a team player. I just... I felt so incredibly confident that my way was right at the time, and I had no patience for anyone questioning it. 

Is that... is that the sort of thing you're asking about? I really hope that doesn't make me sound too awful. I always try to be kind to my coworkers.
